audit.note: binding_call filter on the dialog binding + control_by_id open( searchValue )

deviations.what: handleValueHelp is reproduced 1:1 through two follow-up actions in the order the controller has them: cs_event-binding_call filters the dialog's items binding by NAME Contains the typed value (the model stays untouched, exactly like oValueHelpDialog.getBinding('items').filter([...])), then cs_event-control_by_id open( value ) opens it with that same value in its search field - CONTROL_METHODS declares open's optional string argument, so oValueHelpDialog.open(sInputValue) travels whole. The MultiInput's value is bound two-way so the typed text is on the server when valueHelpRequest fires. The dialog's own search event keeps the roundtrip-free follow_up_action binding_call form (app 103 idiom).

_handleValueHelpClose reads evt.getParameter('selectedItems') and adds one sap.m.Token per item. A list of CONTROLS cannot travel to the backend, so the selection is read from the data instead: the StandardListItem template gains a selected={SELECTED} binding (an added attribute) and the handler loops the rows, appends a token per selected row and clears the flag again. The MultiInput's tokens aggregation is bound to that token table, so the Token in the view is a template the original does not have (it builds Tokens in the controller) - one control more than the original view.xml.

the suggestionItems binding keeps the original's { path, sorter: { path: 'Name' } } shape 1:1 as a raw binding-info string, with the path from client->_bind and the sorter path switched to the ABAP field NAME. The Component's oModel.setSizeLimit(1000000) has no counterpart: an abap2UI5 model carries whatever the ABAP table holds, so all 123 rows are bound without a limit to raise.
